name: Market Category and Positioning Strategy

positioning.oneLineSummary: Tests whether the chosen category gives best-fit customers useful context for differentiated value without imposing false assumptions or excessive education cost.
positioning.productLabel: Market-Category Lens — based on April Dunford's 2026 public materials
notAClaimOf: a novel category always being superior
an aspirational label changing customer perception by itself

attribution.display: Based on April Dunford's 2026 public materials

neutralParaphrase: Choose a category only after alternatives, capability, value, and best-fit customer are understood. Evaluate which category helps the target customer quickly infer what the product is, why its value matters, and which alternatives are relevant; explicitly price the confusion and education burden of an aspirational or new category.

locator.value: 00:00-18:00, aspirational category, category job, three strategies, and new-category risk
Market category follows alternatives, capabilities, value, and best-fit customer
Official learning outcomes: choose the best market including three styles

requiredConditions: OA2-02 through OA2-05 have usable outputs.
Candidate categories can be tested with target customers.
Category assumptions and education cost can be observed.

requiredEvidence.description: What target buyers infer about use case, buyer, features, price, implementation, alternatives, and risk from each category.
Whether the category makes differentiated value easier to understand for best-fit customers.
Time, content, sales effort, budget creation, and risk required to teach or create a category.

decisionQuestions: What assumptions does this category trigger in the target customer's mind?
Do those assumptions illuminate or obscure differentiated value?
Does the company intend to win within, subsegment, or create a category?
Can the company afford the education, budget-creation, and ecosystem burden?
positiveSignals: Best-fit customers understand the product and value faster in the chosen context.
Category assumptions align with real alternatives and buying behavior.
The selected strategy fits company resources and market maturity.
New-category education has a credible budget, channel, and proof plan.
redFlags: The category is aspirational but contradicts customer shortlists.
Sales must repeatedly undo false assumptions created by the label.
Category creation is chosen for uniqueness without an education budget.
Management changes category names while alternatives and value remain unclear.
disconfirmingEvidence: A conventional category improves conversion despite appearing less differentiated.
A subcategory narrows TAM language but makes the company dominant for best-fit buyers.
A new category succeeds because an external market shift already creates demand and language.
Category confusion persists even when the value chain is clear.
contraindications: Do not choose category before OA2-02 through OA2-05.
Do not infer category fit from analyst taxonomy alone.
Do not treat category creation as free differentiation.

instructions: List candidate categories and their customer assumptions.
Compare each with alternatives, value, and best-fit customers.
Conclude aligned, workable with cost, confusing, or insufficient.

deterministicRule.prohibition: The language model must not calculate test effects or market size.

sourceReliability.medium: Customer tests and some sales evidence.
sourceReliability.high: Repeated customer, sales, win/loss, and funnel evidence converge.

evidenceStrength.medium: Improved comprehension with uncertain commercial effect.
evidenceStrength.high: Category repeatedly improves understanding and buying behavior.

evidenceCoverage.high: Alternatives, value, buyers, assumptions, comprehension, conversion, cost, and countercategories covered.

applicabilityConfidence.high: Category materially shapes customer understanding and competition.

promotionRequirements: Review three-strategy definitions in licensed edition.
empiricalQualifications: Category effects vary with market familiarity and distribution.
Tests can be confounded by message quality and sales execution.

rights.notes: Author's public 2026 category guidance is neutrally paraphrased.

openIssues: Verify exact three positioning styles in licensed edition.
